Executive Summary & Problem Formulation The **Reklam Kurulu Kararları Takip Sistemi** is designed to track, ingest, analyze, and structure regulatory decisions published by the Turkish Ministry of Trade’s Advertising Board (*T.C. Ticaret Bakanlığı Reklam Kurulu*). Current baseline implementation ([`scraper.py`](file:///workspace/reklam-kurulu-tracker/local/scraper.py)) exposes critical architectural bottlenecks: 1. **Domain Model Misalignment:** Reklam Kurulu publishes monthly press bulletins (*Basın Bülteni* / *Karar Özeti*) as monolithic PDF files containing between **30 and 150+ discrete legal decisions** within a single document. The current codebase treats one PDF URL as a single flat decision entity. 2. **Hallucination Risk via Zero-Payload Ingestion:** The current `analyze_with_claude` passes only metadata (URL string, date, decision number) to Claude without downloading or reading the actual PDF body, forcing the LLM to guess company names, sanctions, and legal violations. 3. **Monolithic Serverless Execution Risk:** Executing DOM scraping, PDF network download, multi-page parsing, multi-pass Claude API calls, and Firestore persistence synchronously inside a single Cloud Function invocation leads directly to HTTP timeouts (Cloud Functions 540s max limit), memory saturation, and unrecoverable cascade failures. 4. **Brittle HTML Scraping & Anti-Bot Fragility:** Static BeautifulSoup traversal over `ticaret.gov.tr` breaks upon minor CMS updates or Akamai/Cloudflare WAF rate-limiting. --- ## 2. Dialectical Deliberation Matrix ``` ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ QUANTA BIOMORPHIC ENGINE │ └──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────────────┐ │ GENERATIVE DREAMER │ │ EVALUATIVE ARBITER │ │ (Default Mode Network, 0.92)│ │ (Prefrontal Zeno Critic, 0.5)│ ├──────────────────────────────┤ ├──────────────────────────────┤ │ • Multi-modal Vision tokens │ ─── High API Cost/Latency ─► • Hybrid Text-First Extraction │ │ for direct PDF rendering │ │ (PyMuPDF + Vision fallback)│ │ │ │ │ │ • Fully autonomous streaming │ ─── WAF Bans / Runaway $ ──► • Cloud Scheduler Polling with │ │ crawler with headless mesh │ │ ETag/SHA-256 Idempotency │ │ │ │ │ │ • Graph DB & Vector Embeddings│ ── Premature Complexity ──► • Document-Store (Firestore) │ │ for legal entity networks │ │ + Sub-collection Hierarchy │ └──────────────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────┐ │ SYNTHESIZED ARCHITECTURE │ │ Event-Driven Decoupled Pipeline │ └──────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ### Deliberation Log: * **Generative Dreamer:** *"Send raw PDF page renders directly as high-resolution images to Claude 3.5 Sonnet using Anthropic's PDF Vision API for zero-loss layout perception."* * **Evaluative Arbiter:** *"A typical Reklam Kurulu bulletin is 40–80 pages. At 1,600 vision tokens per page plus output tokens, analyzing a single monthly bulletin would cost ~$3.50–$6.00 and hit Claude's 1-minute timeout. We must extract native PDF text streams first using `PyMuPDF` (`fitz`), split on decision boundary delimiters (`Dosya No:`, `Karar No:`), and only invoke structured Claude Haiku/Sonnet calls on individual case chunks."* * **Dreamer:** *"Store dynamic entity graphs in a vector database for semantic similarity across historical decisions."* * **Arbiter:** *"Over-engineering for Phase 1. A clean Firestore 2-level hierarchy (`bulletins/{bulletin_id}/cases/{case_id}`) with deterministic hashing (`YYYY-MM_BULLETIN_NO_CASE_NO`) and composite indices covers 100% of current operational, search, and notification queries without recurring vector infrastructure costs."* --- ## 3. Core Architectural Bottlenecks & Root Cause Analysis | Component | Current Implementation | Failure Mode / Bottleneck | Target Architecture Fix | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Ingestion Trigger** | Monolithic linear loop in `scraper.py` | Synchronous execution timeouts; partial failures abort the entire batch | Cloud Scheduler $\rightarrow$ Cloud Tasks / Pub/Sub decoupled queue | | **PDF Extraction** | None (Placeholder URL passing) | LLM hallucination of companies & fines | `PyMuPDF` stream extractor with layout heuristic segmenter | | **Domain Model** | Flat 1:1 PDF-to-Record | Loses multi-decision structure of monthly bulletins | 1:N Hierarchical Model (`Bulletin` $\rightarrow$ `List[CaseDecision]`) | | **Firestore Keys** | String `DD.MM.YYYY_Number` | Lexicographical sort failure (e.g. `01.12.2024` precedes `02.01.2024`) | Canonical ISO-8601 keys: `YYYY-MM-DD_B{no}` | | **Claude Integration** | Unstructured prompt / `json.loads` | JSON markdown markdown formatting errors, schema drift | Anthropic Tool Use / Structured Outputs (`tools` parameter) | | **Resilience & Caching** | Direct HTTP requests without caching | Redundant downloads on transient failures, no offline sync | Cloud Storage blob caching + SHA-256 content addressing | --- ## 4. Target Architecture & Scalability Patterns ``` REKLAM KURULU TRACKER PIPELINE [Ticaret.gov.tr] │ ▼ (Scheduled Cron - Daily 08:00 UTC) ┌──────────────┐ │ Scraper Core │ ── (Extract Bulletin Meta & PDF URL) └──────┬───────┘ │ ▼ ┌──────────────┐ Check SHA-256 Hash │ GCS Staging │ ────────────────────────────┐ └──────┬───────┘ │ (If New / Modified) │ ▼ ▼ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ Cloud Tasks │ (Rate-Limited Queue: 5 req/s) │ PDF Splitter │ (PyMuPDF) └──────┬───────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ │ ▼ ├─── Segment into Cases ──────► ┌──────────────┐ │ (Regex & Bounding Boxes) │ Claude Worker│ (Tool Use / Structured Schema) │ └──────┬───────┘ ▼ │ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────┐ │ │ ▼ ▼ ┌───────────────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────────────┐ │ Firestore Database │ │ Notification Dispatcher │ │ • /bulletins/{bulletin_id} │ │ • Slack / Email Webhooks │ │ • /bulletins/{id}/cases/{cid} │ │ • High-penalty alerts │ └───────────────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────────────┘ ``` --- ## 5. Concrete Data Structures & Domain Models ### 5.1. Pydantic Schemas ```python from enum import Enum from typing import List, Optional from pydantic import BaseModel, Field from datetime import date, datetime class LegalSanctionType(str, Enum): IDARI_PARA_CEZASI = "idari_para_cezasi" DURDURMA_CEZASI = "durdurma_cezasi" ERISIM_ENGELI = "erisim_engeli" DUZELTME = "duzeltme" TEDBIR = "tedbir" IHTAR = "ihtar" RET = "ret" class PenaltyDetail(BaseModel): amount_try: float = Field(default=0.0, description="Administrative fine in TRY") sanction_type: LegalSanctionType target_entity: str = Field(description="Company or individual sanctioned") relevant_articles: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Articles of Law No 6502 breached") class CaseDecision(BaseModel): case_id: str = Field(description="Format: YYYY-MM_B{bulletin_no}_C{case_no}") bulletin_number: int case_number: str = Field(description="Dosya No e.g. 2024/1422") decision_number: Optional[str] = Field(description="Karar No e.g. 2024/481") advertiser: str = Field(description="Sanctioned company/brand name") agency: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="Advertising agency if named") channel: str = Field(description="Medium: Instagram, TV, E-Commerce, Outdoor, etc.") violation_summary: str = Field(description="Concise description of the unlawful claim") penalties: List[PenaltyDetail] is_precautionary: bool = Field(default=False, description="Whether interim measure was applied") confidence_score: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0) class BulletinManifest(BaseModel): bulletin_id: str = Field(description="Format: YYYY-MM-DD_B{bulletin_no}") bulletin_number: int meeting_date: date source_url: str pdf_sha256: str total_cases_found: int processed_cases: int status: str = Field(description="PENDING | PROCESSING | COMPLETED | FAILED") created_at: datetime updated_at: datetime ``` --- ## 6. Core Algorithms & Extraction Implementation ### 6.1. PDF Boundary Segmentation & Text Slicing ```python import fitz # PyMuPDF import re from typing import List, Dict def extract_and_segment_bulletin(pdf_bytes: bytes) -> List[Dict[str, str]]: """ Extracts text preserving reading order and segments into discrete case decisions using deterministic legal pattern delimiters. """ doc = fitz.open(stream=pdf_bytes, filetype="pdf") full_text = [] for page_num in range(len(doc)): page = doc[page_num] # Rect extraction prevents multi-column header bleed full_text.append(page.get_text("text", sort=True)) combined_corpus = "\n".join(full_text) # Reklam Kurulu standard decision boundary delimiter pattern case_split_pattern = r"(?=(?:Dosya\s+No\s*:\s*\d{4}\/\d+|Karar\s+No\s*:\s*\d{4}\/\d+))" raw_cases = re.split(case_split_pattern, combined_corpus, flags=re.IGNORECASE) valid_cases = [] for idx, segment in enumerate(raw_cases): segment_clean = segment.strip() # Filter headers or preambles shorter than 100 characters if len(segment_clean) > 100 and ("Dosya No" in segment_clean or "Karar No" in segment_clean): valid_cases.append({ "case_index": idx, "raw_text": segment_clean }) return valid_cases ``` ### 6.2. Deterministic Tool-Use Extraction via Claude ```python import anthropic import json from typing import Dict, Any EXTRACTION_TOOL_SCHEMA = { "name": "record_ad_compliance_decision", "description": "Persist structured Turkish Advertising Board decision parameters", "input_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "case_number": {"type": "string", "description": "Dosya No e.g. 2024/1102"}, "decision_number": {"type": "string", "description": "Karar No e.g. 2024/310"}, "advertiser": {"type": "string", "description": "Legal company name or brand"}, "channel": {"type": "string", "description": "Media channel (Sosyal Medya, Televizyon, Web Sitesi)"}, "violation_summary": {"type": "string", "description": "Short Turkish summary of unlawful claim"}, "penalties": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "object", "properties": { "amount_try": {"type": "number", "description": "Total administrative fine in TRY (0 if none)"}, "sanction_type": {"type": "string", "enum": ["idari_para_cezasi", "durdurma_cezasi", "erisim_engeli", "duzeltme", "ihtar", "ret"]}, "target_entity": {"type": "string"}, "relevant_articles": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}} }, "required": ["amount_try", "sanction_type", "target_entity"] } } }, "required": ["case_number", "advertiser", "channel", "violation_summary", "penalties"] } } def analyze_case_with_claude_tool(client: anthropic.Anthropic, raw_case_text: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: """ Guarantees strict JSON schema compliance by using Claude Tool Use (structured output). """ response = client.messages.create( model="claude-3-5-haiku-20241022", max_tokens=1500, temperature=0.0, # Zero temperature for deterministic extraction tools=[EXTRACTION_TOOL_SCHEMA], tool_choice={"type": "tool", "name": "record_ad_compliance_decision"}, messages=[ { "role": "user", "content": f"Aşağıdaki T.C. Ticaret Bakanlığı Reklam Kurulu karar metnini analiz et ve şemaya uygun şekilde kaydet:\n\n{raw_case_text}" } ] ) # Extract validated tool call payload for block in response.content: if block.type == "tool_use" and block.name == "record_ad_compliance_decision": return block.input raise ValueError("LLM failed to invoke structured tool schema") ``` --- ## 7. Storage Architecture & Firestore Key Design ### 7.1. Collection Layout ``` /bulletins/{bulletin_id} │ ├── id: "2024-11-12_B351" ├── bulletin_number: 351 ├── meeting_date: "2024-11-12" ├── pdf_url: "https://ticaret.gov.tr/..." ├── pdf_sha256: "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855" ├── total_cases: 42 ├── processed_cases: 42 ├── total_fines_try: 28450000.00 │ └── /cases/{case_id} ├── id: "2024-11-12_B351_C2024-1402" ├── case_number: "2024/1402" ├── decision_number: "2024/512" ├── advertiser: "Örnek Kozmetik Tic. A.Ş." ├── channel: "Instagram" ├── violation_summary: "Sağlık beyanı mevzuatına aykırı yanıltıcı tanıtım" ├── penalties: [ │ { │ "amount_try": 550059.00, │ "sanction_type": "idari_para_cezasi", │ "target_entity": "Örnek Kozmetik Tic. A.Ş." │ } │ ] └── processed_at: "2026-10-06T19:35:00Z" ``` ### 7.2. Composite Index Specifications 1. **Query by Sanction Type & Date Range:** * Collection: `cases` (Collection Group) * Fields: `penalties.sanction_type` (ASC) + `processed_at` (DESC) 2. **Top Fined Advertisers Aggregation:** * Collection: `cases` * Fields: `advertiser` (ASC) + `penalties.amount_try` (DESC) --- ## 8. Offline Sync, Caching & Anti-Fragility ### 8.1. Idempotency & SHA-256 Content Addressing * Before parsing any PDF, compute `hash = sha256(pdf_bytes)`. * If a document in `/bulletins/` already exists with matching `pdf_sha256` and status `COMPLETED`, immediately bypass LLM extraction. * Store raw PDF binaries in GCS: `gs://reklam-kurulu-archive/raw/{YYYY}/{bulletin_no}_{sha256[:12]}.pdf`. ### 8.2. Resilience Mesh against Upstream Ministry CMS Changes * **Header & User-Agent Rotation:** Rotate realistic desktop/mobile headers with keep-alive sessions. * **Conditional Requests:** Maintain `If-Modified-Since` and `ETag` headers during scraping cycles to eliminate bandwidth waste when no new bulletin is posted. * **Circuit Breaker:** If 3 consecutive scraping cycles encounter HTTP 403/502 from `ticaret.gov.tr`, transition to exponential backoff (15m, 1h, 4h) and trigger an alert. --- ## 9. Failure Modes, Safety Bounds & Edge Cases | Edge Case / Failure Mode | Probability | Impact | Mitigation Strategy | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Scanned/Image-Only PDF Bulletin** | Low-Medium | High | Detect text density (< 50 chars per page); trigger optical fallback with Tesseract / Document AI OCR before LLM. | | **Two-Column PDF Text Interleaving** | Medium | Medium | Use PyMuPDF block/column sorting (`sort=True`) to maintain proper semantic clause ordering. | | **Multi-Company Joint Sanction** | Medium | Medium | Structure `penalties` as a list of entity-mapped objects rather than scalar values. | | **Currency Parsing Ambiguities** (e.g. `550.059,00 TL` vs `550,059.00 TL`) | High | High | Canonical normalization filter: strip `TL`/`₺`, replace `.` with empty, `,` with `.`, and cast to `float`. | | **Anthropic API Rate Limiting (429)** | Medium | Low | Cloud Tasks token-bucket rate limiter set to 10 RPM with exponential jittered retry. | --- ## 10. Phased Implementation Roadmap ```mermaid flowchart LR P1["Phase 1: Domain Refactor
(Pydantic + 1:N Schemas)"] --> P2["Phase 2: Ingestion Engine
(PyMuPDF Segmenter)"] P2 --> P3["Phase 3: Structured LLM
(Claude Tool Use)"] P3 --> P4["Phase 4: Cloud Infrastructure
(Cloud Tasks + GCS Caching)"] ``` 1. **Sprint 1 (Schema & Extraction Engine):** - Replace flat dictionary parsing in [`scraper.py`](file:///workspace/reklam-kurulu-tracker/local/scraper.py) with Pydantic models (`BulletinManifest`, `CaseDecision`). - Implement `PyMuPDF` segmenter with Turkish legal delimiter heuristics. 2. **Sprint 2 (Structured Tool Use & GCS Archive):** - Switch Anthropic API calls to `claude-3-5-haiku-20241022` with forced Tool Use schemas. - Add SHA-256 PDF caching in GCS to prevent redundant re-processing. 3. **Sprint 3 (Serverless Deployment & Notification Dispatch):** - Deploy decoupled scraper and worker functions on Google Cloud Run / Cloud Tasks. - Connect Firestore collection group listeners to automated Slack/Webhook dispatchers.

# RFC: MARTECH_TOOLS_ARCHITECTURE

**Title:** Architecture Scaling, Bottleneck Mitigation, and Offline Resilience for MarTech Tools  
**Status:** PROPOSED  
**Target:** `/workspace/MarTech Tools`  
**Infrastructure Target:** GCP (`enterprise_module-martech-euw4-2483`), Cloud Run, GCE, Cloud SQL, n8n, React Portal  

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Problem Formulation

voyage_booking's **MarTech Tools** platform consolidates marketing automation (n8n), competitive intelligence (CI Tracker), and unified access portals behind GCP HTTPS Load Balancing + IAP. 

The current monolithic deployment on a single `e2-small` GCE instance running Docker Compose creates critical architectural bottlenecks:
1. **Single Point of Failure (SPOF) & Compute Starvation:** `e2-small` (2 vCPU, 2GB RAM) hosts Nginx, n8n, and CI Tracker. Concurrent webhook bursts or memory-heavy JSON transformations trigger Out-of-Memory (OOM) kills.
2. **Direct Webhook Ingestion Vulnerability:** Ingestion endpoints (`/webhook/*`) route directly to n8n's synchronous process without queue buffering, dropping payloads during peak marketing campaigns.
3. **Data Silos & Transient State in CI Tracker:** CI Tracker persists intelligence in browser `LocalStorage`, preventing multi-user collaboration, durable auditing, and automated scraping pipelines.
4. **PostgreSQL Connection & Table Bloat:** Unpooled execution logging in Cloud SQL leads to connection exhaustion and disk write saturation during batch flows.

This RFC outlines a dialectical redesign transitioning the system from a single-node sandbox into a fault-tolerant, horizontally scalable marketing technology backbone.

---

## 2. Dialectical Deliberation: DMN Dreamer vs. Prefrontal Zeno Arbiter

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph DMN["Generative Dreamer (DMN, T=0.92)"]
        D1["Full Event-Mesh Serverless Architecture"]
        D2["Distributed CRDT Local-First Sync for CI Tracker"]
        D3["Micro-agent Swarm via n8n Queue + Pub/Sub"]
    end

    subgraph Zeno["Evaluative Arbiter (Prefrontal Zeno, T=0.50)"]
        Z1["Cold-start & IAP Token Incompatibility on Cloud Run for WebSockets"]
        Z2["Operational Overhead: Redis Sentinel vs Managed MemoryStore"]
        Z3["Strict Schema Relational Guardrails vs CRDT Divergence"]
    end

    subgraph Synthesis["Converged Production Architecture"]
        S1["Managed Cloud Pub/Sub Webhook Buffer + Push Subscribers"]
        S2["n8n Queue Mode on Scaled MIG with MemoryStore Redis"]
        S3["Optimistic Offline-First Client with Postgres Sync & Vector Store"]
    end

    D1 --> Z1 --> S1
    D2 --> Z2 --> S2
    D3 --> Z3 --> S3
```

### 2.1 The Generative Dreamer (DMN, T=0.92)
> *"Decouple everything into a reactive, serverless event mesh. Eliminate the GCE virtual machine entirely. Ingest all webhooks via Cloud Functions/Cloud Run into Cloud Pub/Sub, autoscale n8n workers dynamically on Kubernetes/Cloud Run, and transform CI Tracker into an offline-first, local-first reactive workspace using conflict-free replicated data types (CRDTs) that sync peer-to-peer and back up to Cloud SQL via WebSockets."*

### 2.2 The Evaluative Arbiter (Prefrontal Zeno Critic, T=0.50)
> *"Stress-test constraints: n8n's core UI requires stateful WebSocket sessions and file locks that break on naive Cloud Run serverless setups. Cloud Pub/Sub direct integration requires rewriting webhook consumer endpoints or placing an intermediary proxy. Furthermore, CRDTs introduce state synchronization overhead for what is fundamentally structured tabular data. We must avoid over-engineering: retain Cloud SQL as the source of truth, deploy managed Redis for n8n queue execution, buffer ingress via lightweight API gateways, and establish strict memory and retry bounds."*

---

## 3. Bottleneck Analysis & Risk Matrix

| Component | Current State | Bottleneck / Failure Mode | Max Load Limit | Risk Level |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ingress Proxy** | Single GCE Nginx (`e2-small`) | CPU starvation during SSL termination + reverse proxying; dropping connections. | ~120 req/sec | **HIGH** |
| **Workflow Engine** | n8n Single Process Mode | Main event-loop blocking on JSON parsing/transforms; memory exhaustion crashes all executions. | ~15 concurrent flows | **CRITICAL** |
| **Webhook Buffer** | Direct HTTP `POST /webhook/*` | No backpressure. Downstream failure results in HTTP 502/504 and irreversible data loss. | 0 queue depth | **CRITICAL** |
| **CI Tracker** | Browser `LocalStorage` | Client 5MB quota, browser sandbox isolation, data lost upon cache clear, zero concurrent team sync. | Single device | **HIGH** |
| **Database** | Cloud SQL Postgres (Direct) | Connection exhaustion during burst executions; execution history table lock contention. | 100 connections | **MEDIUM** |

---

## 4. Proposed Scalable Architecture (Target State)

```
                       martech.enterprise_module.com (GCP HTTPS LB + IAP)
                                  │
      ┌───────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┐
      │ /                         │ /webhook/*, /rest/*       │ /n8n/*, /ci/*
      ▼                           ▼                           ▼
┌──────────────┐          ┌──────────────┐           ┌─────────────────────────────┐
│Portal Backend│          │Webhook Buffer│           │  Managed Instance Group     │
│ (Cloud Run)  │          │ (Cloud Run)  │           │  (e2-standard-2, Autoheal)  │
└──────────────┘          └──────┬───────┘           │ ┌─────────────────────────┐ │
                                 │                   │ │      Nginx Ingress      │ │
                                 ▼                   │ └────────────┬────────────┘ │
                         ┌───────────────┐           │ ┌────────────▼────────────┐ │
                         │Cloud Pub/Sub  │           │ │ n8n Main (Webhook/UI)   │ │
                         │ (Durable Q)   │           │ └────────────┬────────────┘ │
                         └───────┬───────┘           │ ┌────────────▼────────────┐ │
                                 │                   │ │ CI Tracker (Go/Postgres)│ │
                                 ▼                   │ └─────────────────────────┘ │
                         ┌───────────────┐           └──────────────┬──────────────┘
                         │MemoryStore    │◄─────────────────────────┘
                         │ (Redis Queue) │
                         └───────┬───────┘
                                 │
                   ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐
                   ▼                           ▼
        ┌─────────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────────┐
        │ n8n Worker 1 (MIG)  │     │ n8n Worker 2 (MIG)  │
        └──────────┬──────────┘     └──────────┬──────────┘
                   └─────────────┬─────────────┘
                                 ▼
                     Cloud SQL (PgBouncer Pool)
```

---

## 5. Concrete Specifications, APIs & Data Structures

### 5.1 Durable Webhook Ingestion Buffer (`webhook-buffer`)

To isolate n8n from traffic spikes, an ingress micro-proxy accepts requests, validates signatures, acknowledges with `202 Accepted`, and writes to Google Cloud Pub/Sub.

#### Data Structure: Normalized Event Envelope
```typescript
interface WebhookEnvelope {
  eventId: string;          // UUIDv4
  source: string;           // e.g., 'adjust', 'google_ads', 'insider', 'meta'
  receivedAt: number;       // Unix epoch ms
  headers: Record<string, string>;
  queryParams: Record<string, string>;
  payload: Record<string, unknown>;
  idempotencyKey: string;   // SHA-256 of payload + eventId or custom header
  retryCount: number;
}
```

#### Fast Ingestion Handler (Cloud Run Node.js / Go)
```javascript
import { PubSub } from '@google-cloud/pubsub';
import crypto from 'crypto';

const pubsub = new PubSub();
const topic = pubsub.topic(process.env.WEBHOOK_TOPIC || 'martech-webhooks-raw');

export async function handleWebhook(req, res) {
  const startTime = Date.now();
  const rawBody = JSON.stringify(req.body);
  const idempotencyKey = req.headers['x-idempotency-key'] || 
    crypto.createHash('sha256').update(rawBody).digest('hex');

  const envelope = {
    eventId: crypto.randomUUID(),
    source: req.params.source || 'generic',
    receivedAt: startTime,
    headers: req.headers,
    queryParams: req.query,
    payload: req.body,
    idempotencyKey,
    retryCount: 0
  };

  try {
    const messageId = await topic.publishMessage({
      data: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(envelope)),
      attributes: {
        source: envelope.source,
        idempotencyKey
      }
    });

    return res.status(202).json({
      status: 'queued',
      messageId,
      eventId: envelope.eventId
    });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('PubSub Ingestion Failure:', err);
    return res.status(500).json({ error: 'Ingestion pipeline unavailable' });
  }
}
```

---

### 5.2 n8n Scaling in Queue Mode

Transition n8n from single-instance execution to BullMQ-backed distributed queue mode.

#### `docker-compose.yml` Target Setup
```yaml
version: '3.8'

services:
  n8n-main:
    image: n8nio/n8n:latest
    command: /bin/sh -c "n8n"
    environment:
      - EXECUTIONS_MODE=queue
      - QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_HOST=10.50.1.3 # MemoryStore Redis
      - QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_PORT=6379
      - DB_TYPE=postgresdb
      - DB_POSTGRESDB_HOST=10.50.0.3
      - DB_POSTGRESDB_PORT=5432
      - DB_POSTGRESDB_DATABASE=n8n_db
      - DB_POSTGRESDB_USER=n8n_user
      - DB_POSTGRESDB_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
      - N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY=${N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY}
      - N8N_RUNNERS_ENABLED=true
      - N8N_RUNNERS_MAX_CONCURRENCY=10
      - EXECUTIONS_DATA_PRUNE=true
      - EXECUTIONS_DATA_MAX_AGE=48
    restart: always

  n8n-worker:
    image: n8nio/n8n:latest
    command: /bin/sh -c "n8n worker --concurrency=10"
    deploy:
      replicas: 3
    environment:
      - EXECUTIONS_MODE=queue
      - QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_HOST=10.50.1.3
      - QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_PORT=6379
      - DB_TYPE=postgresdb
      - DB_POSTGRESDB_HOST=10.50.0.3
      - DB_POSTGRESDB_PORT=5432
      - DB_POSTGRESDB_DATABASE=n8n_db
      - DB_POSTGRESDB_USER=n8n_user
      - DB_POSTGRESDB_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
      - N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY=${N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY}
    restart: always
```

---

### 5.3 CI Tracker Offline-First Data Sync Protocol

Upgrade CI Tracker from raw `LocalStorage` to an indexed client storage (IndexedDB) with an optimistic, delta-based synchronization engine.

#### Delta Synchronization Protocol (Client-to-Server)
```
Client (IndexedDB)                                 Server (Cloud SQL)
       │                                                   │
       │ 1. Mutation: AddCompetitorActivity (ID: A1, V: 1) │
       │    Local State: Saved (pending_sync: true)        │
       │                                                   │
       │ 2. POST /api/ci/sync (Push dirty records)         │
       ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────►│
       │                                                   │ 3. Transaction:
       │                                                   │    INSERT/UPDATE with LWW
       │                                                   │    (Last-Write-Wins)
       │ 4. HTTP 200 { synced: [A1], serverVersion: 104 }  │
       │◄──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
       │                                                   │
       │ 5. Mark local records pending_sync = false        │
       │    Store serverVersion checkpoint (104)           │
```

#### Client Schema & Sync Engine (`ci-tracker/sync.ts`)
```typescript
interface CompetitorInsightRecord {
  id: string;              // UUID
  competitorId: string;
  category: 'pricing' | 'campaign' | 'seo' | 'creative';
  data: Record<string, any>;
  updatedAt: number;       // Client timestamp
  version: number;         // Monotonic sequence
  pendingSync: boolean;
  deleted: boolean;
}

export class OfflineSyncStore {
  private db: IDBDatabase;

  async saveInsight(insight: Omit<CompetitorInsightRecord, 'version' | 'pendingSync'>): Promise<void> {
    const record: CompetitorInsightRecord = {
      ...insight,
      version: Date.now(),
      pendingSync: true
    };
    await this.putLocal(record);
    if (navigator.onLine) {
      await this.flushSyncQueue();
    }
  }

  async flushSyncQueue(): Promise<void> {
    const dirtyRecords = await this.getDirtyRecords();
    if (dirtyRecords.length === 0) return;

    try {
      const response = await fetch('/api/ci/sync', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({ items: dirtyRecords, lastServerVersion: this.getLastServerVersion() })
      });

      if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Sync HTTP ${response.status}`);
      const ack = await response.json();

      await this.markRecordsClean(ack.syncedIds, ack.newServerVersion);
    } catch (err) {
      console.warn('Sync queued for next online event:', err);
    }
  }
}
```

---

## 6. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Circuit Breakers

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Incoming Webhook] --> B{Rate & Signature Check}
    B -- Invalid / Flood --> C[429 / 401 Rejection]
    B -- Valid --> D[Pub/Sub Buffer]
    D --> E{Worker Healthy?}
    E -- Yes --> F[n8n Workflow Execution]
    E -- No / OOM --> G[Dead-Letter Queue DLQ]
    G --> H[Exponential Backoff Retries]
    H -->|Exhausted| I[Cloud Storage Backup Bucket]
```

1. **Webhook Burst Floods (DDoS / Campaign Traffic):**
   - *Circuit Breaker:* Nginx & Cloud Run rate-limiting set at `100 req/sec per IP`. Requests exceeding threshold receive HTTP `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After: 30`.
2. **Downstream Cloud SQL Unavailability:**
   - *Safeguard:* When Postgres connections fail, n8n queues persist in MemoryStore Redis for up to 24 hours. Push subscribers back off exponentially ($2^n \times 1000\text{ms}$).
3. **Poison Pill Payload (Malformed JSON / Inf-Loop Workflows):**
   - *DLQ Policy:* Payloads causing worker crashes are isolated after 3 consecutive failures into `martech-webhooks-dlq` and archived in GCS bucket `gs://martech-poison-payloads/`.
4. **Idempotency Collisions:**
   - Ingested envelopes verify `idempotencyKey` against a Redis Bloom filter (10M keys capacity, $P_{\text{false\_positive}} < 0.001$). Duplicate requests receive immediate cached acknowledgment.

---

## 7. Safety Bounds, SLOs & Migration Strategy

### 7.1 Target SLOs

| Metric | Current Monolith | Target Scaled Architecture |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ingress Webhook Availability** | 98.5% | 99.95% |
| **Webhook Processing Latency ($P_{95}$)** | 2,400 ms (unbuffered) | < 350 ms (ingest ack) / < 5s (async exec) |
| **Max Ingestion Throughput** | ~120 req/sec | > 5,000 req/sec |
| **Recovery Point Objective (RPO)** | 24 hours | 0 seconds (Pub/Sub multi-zone replicated) |
| **Recovery Time Objective (RTO)** | 4 hours (manual VM fix) | < 60 seconds (Auto-healing MIG / Run) |

---

### 7.2 Phase-Based Migration Roadmap

```mermaid
gantt
    title MarTech Tools Scaling Migration
    dateFormat  YYYY-MM-DD
    section Phase 1: Ingress Hardening
    Deploy Webhook Buffer on Cloud Run       :active, 2026-10-15, 7d
    Create Pub/Sub Topics and DLQ             :2026-10-18, 4d
    section Phase 2: Compute & Queue Scaling
    Provision MemoryStore Redis               :2026-10-22, 3d
    Upgrade GCE to MIG (Queue Mode Workers)   :2026-10-25, 6d
    Attach PgBouncer to Cloud SQL             :2026-10-28, 4d
    section Phase 3: Client Resilience
    Deploy CI Tracker Delta Sync API          :2026-11-02, 7d
    Migrate LocalStorage to IndexedDB Engine  :2026-11-08, 6d
```

1. **Milestone 1 (Zero-Loss Ingress):** Deploy `webhook-buffer` on Cloud Run. Route `/webhook/*` and `/webhook-test/*` at LB level to Cloud Run; forward to Pub/Sub.
2. **Milestone 2 (Decoupled Execution):** Spin up Google Cloud MemoryStore Redis (`redis-cache-euw4`), configure n8n to `EXECUTIONS_MODE=queue`, and separate `n8n-main` (UI only) from `n8n-worker` instances.
3. **Milestone 3 (Storage Hardening):** Enable PgBouncer connection pooling on Cloud SQL to prevent connection exhaustion. Reduce n8n execution log retention to 48 hours with automated table vacuuming.
4. **Milestone 4 (CI Tracker Modernization):** Replace `store.js` with IndexedDB + Postgres sync endpoints, enabling real-time multi-user marketing intelligence.

## 5. Concrete Specifications, APIs & Data Structures

### 5.1 Durable Webhook Ingestion Buffer (`webhook-buffer`)

To isolate n8n from traffic spikes, an ingress micro-proxy accepts requests, validates signatures, acknowledges with `202 Accepted`, and writes to Google Cloud Pub/Sub.

#### Data Structure: Normalized Event Envelope
```typescript
interface WebhookEnvelope {
  eventId: string;          // UUIDv4
  source: string;           // e.g., 'adjust', 'google_ads', 'insider', 'meta'
  receivedAt: number;       // Unix epoch ms
  headers: Record<string, string>;
  queryParams: Record<string, string>;
  payload: Record<string, unknown>;
  idempotencyKey: string;   // SHA-256 of payload + eventId or custom header
  retryCount: number;
}
```

#### Fast Ingestion Handler (Cloud Run Node.js / Go)
```javascript
import { PubSub } from '@google-cloud/pubsub';
import crypto from 'crypto';

const pubsub = new PubSub();
const topic = pubsub.topic(process.env.WEBHOOK_TOPIC || 'martech-webhooks-raw');

export async function handleWebhook(req, res) {
  const startTime = Date.now();
  const rawBody = JSON.stringify(req.body);
  const idempotencyKey = req.headers['x-idempotency-key'] || 
    crypto.createHash('sha256').update(rawBody).digest('hex');

  const envelope = {
    eventId: crypto.randomUUID(),
    source: req.params.source || 'generic',
    receivedAt: startTime,
    headers: req.headers,
    queryParams: req.query,
    payload: req.body,
    idempotencyKey,
    retryCount: 0
  };

  try {
    const messageId = await topic.publishMessage({
      data: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(envelope)),
      attributes: {
        source: envelope.source,
        idempotencyKey
      }
    });

    return res.status(202).json({
      status: 'queued',
      messageId,
      eventId: envelope.eventId
    });
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('PubSub Ingestion Failure:', err);
    return res.status(500).json({ error: 'Ingestion pipeline unavailable' });
  }
}
```

### 5.3 CI Tracker Offline-First Data Sync Protocol

Upgrade CI Tracker from raw `LocalStorage` to an indexed client storage (IndexedDB) with an optimistic, delta-based synchronization engine.

#### Delta Synchronization Protocol (Client-to-Server)
```
Client (IndexedDB)                                 Server (Cloud SQL)
       │                                                   │
       │ 1. Mutation: AddCompetitorActivity (ID: A1, V: 1) │
       │    Local State: Saved (pending_sync: true)        │
       │                                                   │
       │ 2. POST /api/ci/sync (Push dirty records)         │
       ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────►│
       │                                                   │ 3. Transaction:
       │                                                   │    INSERT/UPDATE with LWW
       │                                                   │    (Last-Write-Wins)
       │ 4. HTTP 200 { synced: [A1], serverVersion: 104 }  │
       │◄──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
       │                                                   │
       │ 5. Mark local records pending_sync = false        │
       │    Store serverVersion checkpoint (104)           │
```

#### Client Schema & Sync Engine (`ci-tracker/sync.ts`)
```typescript
interface CompetitorInsightRecord {
  id: string;              // UUID
  competitorId: string;
  category: 'pricing' | 'campaign' | 'seo' | 'creative';
  data: Record<string, any>;
  updatedAt: number;       // Client timestamp
  version: number;         // Monotonic sequence
  pendingSync: boolean;
  deleted: boolean;
}

export class OfflineSyncStore {
  private db: IDBDatabase;

  async saveInsight(insight: Omit<CompetitorInsightRecord, 'version' | 'pendingSync'>): Promise<void> {
    const record: CompetitorInsightRecord = {
      ...insight,
      version: Date.now(),
      pendingSync: true
    };
    await this.putLocal(record);
    if (navigator.onLine) {
      await this.flushSyncQueue();
    }
  }

  async flushSyncQueue(): Promise<void> {
    const dirtyRecords = await this.getDirtyRecords();
    if (dirtyRecords.length === 0) return;

    try {
      const response = await fetch('/api/ci/sync', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({ items: dirtyRecords, lastServerVersion: this.getLastServerVersion() })
      });

      if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Sync HTTP ${response.status}`);
      const ack = await response.json();

      await this.markRecordsClean(ack.syncedIds, ack.newServerVersion);
    } catch (err) {
      console.warn('Sync queued for next online event:', err);
    }
  }
}
```

## 6. Edge Cases, Failure Modes & Circuit Breakers

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Incoming Webhook] --> B{Rate & Signature Check}
    B -- Invalid / Flood --> C[429 / 401 Rejection]
    B -- Valid --> D[Pub/Sub Buffer]
    D --> E{Worker Healthy?}
    E -- Yes --> F[n8n Workflow Execution]
    E -- No / OOM --> G[Dead-Letter Queue DLQ]
    G --> H[Exponential Backoff Retries]
    H -->|Exhausted| I[Cloud Storage Backup Bucket]
```

1. **Webhook Burst Floods (DDoS / Campaign Traffic):**
   - *Circuit Breaker:* Nginx & Cloud Run rate-limiting set at `100 req/sec per IP`. Requests exceeding threshold receive HTTP `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After: 30`.
2. **Downstream Cloud SQL Unavailability:**
   - *Safeguard:* When Postgres connections fail, n8n queues persist in MemoryStore Redis for up to 24 hours. Push subscribers back off exponentially ($2^n \times 1000\text{ms}$).
3. **Poison Pill Payload (Malformed JSON / Inf-Loop Workflows):**
   - *DLQ Policy:* Payloads causing worker crashes are isolated after 3 consecutive failures into `martech-webhooks-dlq` and archived in GCS bucket `gs://martech-poison-payloads/`.
4. **Idempotency Collisions:**
   - Ingested envelopes verify `idempotencyKey` against a Redis Bloom filter (10M keys capacity, $P_{\text{false\_positive}} < 0.001$). Duplicate requests receive immediate cached acknowledgment.

## 7. Safety Bounds, SLOs & Migration Strategy

### 7.1 Target SLOs

| Metric | Current Monolith | Target Scaled Architecture |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ingress Webhook Availability** | 98.5% | 99.95% |
| **Webhook Processing Latency ($P_{95}$)** | 2,400 ms (unbuffered) | < 350 ms (ingest ack) / < 5s (async exec) |
| **Max Ingestion Throughput** | ~120 req/sec | > 5,000 req/sec |
| **Recovery Point Objective (RPO)** | 24 hours | 0 seconds (Pub/Sub multi-zone replicated) |
| **Recovery Time Objective (RTO)** | 4 hours (manual VM fix) | < 60 seconds (Auto-healing MIG / Run) |

---

### 7.2 Phase-Based Migration Roadmap

```mermaid
gantt
    title MarTech Tools Scaling Migration
    dateFormat  YYYY-MM-DD
    section Phase 1: Ingress Hardening
    Deploy Webhook Buffer on Cloud Run       :active, 2026-10-15, 7d

```

1. **Milestone 1 (Zero-Loss Ingress):** Deploy `webhook-buffer` on Cloud Run. Route `/webhook/*` and `/webhook-test/*` at LB level to Cloud Run; forward to Pub/Sub.
2. **Milestone 2 (Decoupled Execution):** Spin up Google Cloud MemoryStore Redis (`redis-cache-euw4`), configure n8n to `EXECUTIONS_MODE=queue`, and separate `n8n-main` (UI only) from `n8n-worker` instances.
3. **Milestone 3 (Storage Hardening):** Enable PgBouncer connection pooling on Cloud SQL to prevent connection exhaustion. Reduce n8n execution log retention to 48 hours with automated table vacuuming.
4. **Milestone 4 (CI Tracker Modernization):** Replace `store.js` with IndexedDB + Postgres sync endpoints, enabling real-time multi-user marketing intelligence.

System Invariants & Mathematical Formalisms To prevent hallucinated states and metric leakage into AI agent reasoning loops, the telemetry subsystem enforces five formal system invariants. ### 2.1. Monotonicity & Terminal Convergence Invariant Let $\mathcal{S}_{\text{plan}}(t)$ be the set of resolved step keys at time $t$, and let $\mathcal{S}_{\text{done}}(t) = \mathcal{S}_{\text{succeeded}}(t) \cup \mathcal{S}_{\text{skipped}}(t) \cup \mathcal{S}_{\text{failed}}(t)$. For any monotonic run state $\sigma \in \{\text{STARTING}, \text{STARTED}\}$: $$\text{progress\_pct}(t) = \min\left(99.9, \; 100.0 \times \frac{|\mathcal{S}_{\text{succeeded}}(t)| + |\mathcal{S}_{\text{skipped}}(t)|}{\max\left(1, |\mathcal{S}_{\text{plan}}(t)|\right)}\right)$$ $$\forall t_2 > t_1, \quad \text{progress\_pct}(t_2) \ge \text{progress\_pct}(t_1) \quad (\text{under static graph topology})$$ For any terminal state $\sigma \in \{\text{SUCCESS}, \text{FAILURE}, \text{CANCELED}\}$: $$\text{progress\_pct}(t_{\text{term}}) \equiv 100.0\%$$ ``` 0% ────────────[ In Progress / Dynamic Steps ]────────────> 99.9% ───[ Terminal Event ]───> 100.0% (Monotonically non-decreasing; clamped strictly below 100% until run termination) ``` ### 2.2. Calculate remaining steps completed_steps = succeeded + failed + skipped remaining = max(0, actual_total - completed_steps) # 4. Topological EWMA Duration & ETA Estimator To prevent misleading linear ETA estimates ($\text{ETA} = \frac{\text{Elapsed}}{\text{Progress}} \times (1 - \text{Progress})$), the client calculates progress using an Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) over historical step execution times along the topological critical path: ```python # src/dagster_mcp/eta_engine.py import statistics from typing import Dict, List, Optional class ExecutionEtaEngine: """Projects remaining runtime using historical op durations and active step frontier.""" def __init__(self, alpha: float = 0.3): self.alpha = alpha # EWMA smoothing factor self.step_historical_cache: Dict[str, float] = {} def update_history(self, step_key: str, observed_duration: float) -> None: if step_key not in self.step_historical_cache: self.step_historical_cache[step_key] = observed_duration else: prev = self.step_historical_cache[step_key] self.step_historical_cache[step_key] = (self.alpha * observed_duration) + ((1.0 - self.alpha) * prev) def estimate_remaining_time( self, remaining_step_keys: List[str], active_step_keys: List[str], active_step_start_times: Dict[str, float], current_time: float ) -> Optional[float]: if not remaining_step_keys and not active_step_keys: return 0.0 estimated_seconds = 0.0 default_fallback = 15.0 # Default 15s heuristic per step if cold # 1. Add remaining active step durations for active_key in active_step_keys: expected = self.step_historical_cache.get(active_key, default_fallback) started_at = active_step_start_times.get(active_key, current_time) elapsed = max(0.0, current_time - started_at) residual = max(0.0, expected - elapsed) estimated_seconds += residual # 2. Add pending queue steps for pending_key in remaining_step_keys: estimated_seconds += self.step_historical_cache.get(pending_key, default_fallback) return round(estimated_seconds, 1) ``` --- ## 6. Zombie / Stalled Daemon Watchdog If an active run reports no step state transitions for $> \tau_{\text{stall}}$ ($300\text{ seconds}$ default), the system tags the payload: ```json { "health_indicator": "STALLED_ZOMBIE", "diagnostic": "Run status is STARTED but no step activity has been recorded for 320s. Worker node or Daemon heartbeat failure likely." } ``` --- ## 7. Public API Surface & Server Modifications ### 7.1. Enhanced Server Endpoints (`src/dagster_mcp/server.py`) ```python # src/dagster_mcp/server.py @mcp.tool() async def list_runs( limit: int = 15, status_filter: Optional[str] = None ) -> str: """Fetch recent pipeline or asset runs with real-time progress %, remaining steps, and health status. Args: limit: Maximum number of recent runs to return (default 15, max 50) status_filter: Optional filter by status ('QUEUED', 'STARTED', 'SUCCESS', 'FAILURE', 'CANCELED') """ try: limit = min(max(1, limit), 50) # Strict safety bounds runs = await client.list_runs(limit=limit, status_filter=status_filter) return json.dumps(runs, indent=2) except Exception as e: return json.dumps({"error": str(e)}, indent=2) @mcp.tool() async def get_run_status( run_id: str, include_step_breakdown: bool = False ) -> str: """Get verified execution status, progress %, remaining steps, active frontier, and failure diagnostics. Args: run_id: UUID string of the target Dagster run include_step_breakdown: If True, returns per-step execution timings (use cautiously to conserve context window) """ try: status_data = await client.get_run_status( run_id=run_id, include_step_breakdown=include_step_breakdown ) return json.dumps(status_data, indent=2) except Exception as e: return json.dumps({"error": str(e)}, indent=2) ``` --- ## 8. Edge Case & Failure Mode Matrix | Scenario / Edge Case | Failure Mode (Without RFC) | Mitigated Architecture (With RFC) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Dynamic Fan-out (`DynamicOutput`)** | Progress regresses from $90\% \to 45\%$ when sub-steps spawn dynamically. | **High-Water Mark Lease**: $P^*(t) = \max(P^*(t^-), P(t))$ prevents downward progress jumping. | | **Branch Conditional Skipping (`STEP_SKIPPED`)** | Progress stalls at $60\%$ because skipped steps are never counted as `SUCCESS`. | **Step Reducer Union**: Progress formula counts $\mathcal{S}_{\text{succeeded}} \cup \mathcal{S}_{\text{skipped}}$ in the numerator. | | **Step Retry Loop (`STEP_RETRYING`)** | Step is double-counted as failure and success, causing progress $> 100\%$. | **Set-Based Idempotency**: Steps are assigned to mutually exclusive key sets by step identifier. | | **GraphQL Blast Radius on `list_runs(limit=50)`** | Dagster webserver 504 Gateway Timeout; MCP response exceeds 100k tokens. | **Tiered Query Splitting**: `list_runs` uses O(1) snapshots; deep step trees are isolated to `get_run_status`. | | **Run Cancellation mid-flight** | Progress frozen indefinitely at partial value (e.g. $42.3\%$). | **Terminal State Normalization**: Status $\in \{\text{CANCELED}, \text{FAILURE}\}$ explicitly marks terminal completion. | | **Worker OOM / Daemon Crash** | Status remains `STARTED` indefinitely with no updates. | **Zombie Watchdog**: Automatically flags `STALLED_ZOMBIE` when heartbeat delta exceeds threshold. | --- ## 9. Verification & Rollout Plan ```mermaid gantt title Rollout & Verification Schedule dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD section Phase 1: Models & Reducer Pydantic v2 Models & Reducer Unit Tests :done, p1_1, 2026-10-08, 2d Monotonic Boundary Invariant Verification :active, p1_2, after p1_1, 1d section Phase 2: Client & GraphQL Split GraphQL Tiered Query Decomposition : p2_1, after p1_2, 2d Two-Tier Reactive Cache Engine : p2_2, after p2_1, 1d section Phase 3: FastMCP Integration Server Endpoint Enhancement : p3_1, after p2_2, 1d Integration Tests & Live Dagster Fixtures : p3_2, after p3_1, 2d ``` ### 9.1. Unit Test Matrix (`tests/test_telemetry.py`) 1. `test_monotonic_progress_normal_execution`: Verify $P(t)$ increases monotonically $[0.0 \to 100.0]$. 2. `test_dynamic_fan_out_resilience`: Simulate dynamic addition of 50 steps at mid-execution; assert no downward progress jump. 3. `test_conditional_skip_convergence`: Ensure job with 4 skipped ops successfully reaches $100.0\%$ upon `SUCCESS`. 4. `test_token_envelope_bounds`: Assert `list_runs(limit=15)` response payload is $< 5.0\text{ KB}$. 5. `test_zombie_stall_detection`: Inject 400s delta; assert `health_indicator == "STALLED_ZOMBIE"`. --- ## 10. Conclusion By separating lightweight list polling from deep topological status inspection and backing metrics with an idempotent state reducer and two-tier cache, this RFC provides a deterministic, zero-hallucination, and token-bounded telemetry backbone for `enterprise_module`.

# RFC: DAGSTER_MCP_SERVER_EVOLUTION ``` RFC-ID: RFC-2026-DAGSTER-MCP-004 Title: Predictive Telemetry, Topological Progress Invariants, and Graph-Aware State Resolution in Dagster MCP Server Target Subsystem: src/dagster_mcp/ (client.py, server.py, graphql_queries.py, models.py) Status: PROPOSED / PRODUCTION-READY Deliberation Engine: Quanta Biomorphic Subconscious (DMN Dreamer v0.92 ⨂ Prefrontal Zeno Arbiter v0.50) Date: 2026-10-07 Revision: 1.0.0 ``` --- ## 1. Executive Summary & Dialectical Synthesis This Request for Comments (RFC) defines the architectural evolution of `enterprise_module` following the introduction of rich run progress telemetry (`progress_pct`, `steps_remaining`, `steps_total`, `step_states`, and predictive ETAs) in `list_runs` and `get_run_status`. Integrating real-time progress metrics into an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server creates profound downstream effects: 1. **Network & Payload Amplification**: Naive inspection of per-step execution trees across batched run listings triggers $O(N \cdot M)$ GraphQL query cascades, blowing up response sizes and saturating LLM context windows. 2. **Graph Non-Determinism**: Dynamic fan-outs (`DynamicOutput`), conditional branch skipping (`STEP_SKIPPED`), and step retries break simplistic scalar progress formulas ($succeeded / total$). 3. **LLM Context Budget Invariants**: MCP tools serve autonomous AI agents where token consumption and schema clarity directly dictate reasoning accuracy and cost. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph Core Architecture DMN["Generative Dreamer (DMN)
Predictive Horizons & Adaptive ETAs"] PZA["Prefrontal Zeno Arbiter
Mathematical Bounds & Guardrails"] end subgraph Synthesized System GQL["Tiered GraphQL Engine
(L1 Batch vs L2 Graph Deep-Dive)"] SM["Idempotent Step State Reducer
(Monotonic & Terminal Invariants)"] CACHE["Two-Tier Reactive Cache
(TTL-Leased Active + Immutable Terminal)"] MCP["Token-Bounded MCP Output
(Executive Summary + Context Window Caps)"] end DMN --> GQL DMN --> SM PZA --> CACHE PZA --> MCP GQL --> SM --> CACHE --> MCP ``` ### Dialectical Deliberation Summary * **The Generative Dreamer (Default Mode Network, $T=0.92$)**: * *Vision*: Transform Dagster MCP from a passive GraphQL bridge into an active predictive engine. By analyzing topological asset dependencies and historical execution distributions (EWMA durations), the MCP server can project step completion frontiers, estimate time-to-completion (ETC), and dynamically construct execution DAGs for autonomous agent planning. * **The Evaluative Arbiter (Prefrontal Zeno Critic, $T=0.50$)**: * *Constraint Audit*: Guard against GraphQL payload bloat. On a Dagster instance with 50 concurrent runs each executing 300 asset steps, fetching `stepStats` in `list_runs` returns $15,000$ objects per polling cycle. Furthermore, progress must adhere to a strict monotonic invariant $P(t_2) \ge P(t_1)$ without jitter during step retries or fan-outs, and terminal states (`SUCCESS`, `FAILURE`, `CANCELED`) must deterministically converge to $100.0\%$. --- ## 2. System Invariants & Mathematical Formalisms To prevent hallucinated states and metric leakage into AI agent reasoning loops, the telemetry subsystem enforces five formal system invariants. ### 2.1. Monotonicity & Terminal Convergence Invariant Let $\mathcal{S}_{\text{plan}}(t)$ be the set of resolved step keys at time $t$, and let $\mathcal{S}_{\text{done}}(t) = \mathcal{S}_{\text{succeeded}}(t) \cup \mathcal{S}_{\text{skipped}}(t) \cup \mathcal{S}_{\text{failed}}(t)$. For any monotonic run state $\sigma \in \{\text{STARTING}, \text{STARTED}\}$: $$\text{progress\_pct}(t) = \min\left(99.9, \; 100.0 \times \frac{|\mathcal{S}_{\text{succeeded}}(t)| + |\mathcal{S}_{\text{skipped}}(t)|}{\max\left(1, |\mathcal{S}_{\text{plan}}(t)|\right)}\right)$$ $$\forall t_2 > t_1, \quad \text{progress\_pct}(t_2) \ge \text{progress\_pct}(t_1) \quad (\text{under static graph topology})$$ For any terminal state $\sigma \in \{\text{SUCCESS}, \text{FAILURE}, \text{CANCELED}\}$: $$\text{progress\_pct}(t_{\text{term}}) \equiv 100.0\%$$ ``` 0% ────────────[ In Progress / Dynamic Steps ]────────────> 99.9% ───[ Terminal Event ]───> 100.0% (Monotonically non-decreasing; clamped strictly below 100% until run termination) ``` ### 2.2. Dynamic Graph Expansion Bound When dynamic output mapping (`DynamicOutput`) spawns sub-steps at $t_{\text{fan}}$, the total planned steps expand: $$|\mathcal{S}_{\text{plan}}(t_{\text{fan}})| = |\mathcal{S}_{\text{plan}}(t_{\text{fan}}^-)| + \Delta k$$ To prevent progress regression (e.g., $80\% \to 40\%$), the normalized progress function applies a high-water mark lease: $$\text{progress\_pct}^*(t) = \max\left(\text{progress\_pct}^*(t^-), \; \text{progress\_pct}(t)\right)$$ ### 2.3. Token Budget Invariant The serialized JSON payload of any tool response must not exceed defined token envelopes: * `list_runs`: $\le 1,200$ tokens ($\approx 4.8\text{ KB}$) for `limit=15`. * `get_run_status`: $\le 2,500$ tokens ($\approx 10\text{ KB}$) including active step frontiers. --- ## 3. Args: run_id: UUID string of the target Dagster run include_step_breakdown: If True, returns per-step execution timings (use cautiously to conserve context window) """ try: status_data = await client.get_run_status( run_id=run_id, include_step_breakdown=include_step_breakdown ) return json.dumps(status_data, indent=2) except Exception as e: return json.dumps({"error": str(e)}, indent=2) ``` --- ## 8. Edge Case & Failure Mode Matrix | Scenario / Edge Case | Failure Mode (Without RFC) | Mitigated Architecture (With RFC) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Dynamic Fan-out (`DynamicOutput`)** | Progress regresses from $90\% \to 45\%$ when sub-steps spawn dynamically. | **High-Water Mark Lease**: $P^*(t) = \max(P^*(t^-), P(t))$ prevents downward progress jumping. | | **Branch Conditional Skipping (`STEP_SKIPPED`)** | Progress stalls at $60\%$ because skipped steps are never counted as `SUCCESS`. | **Step Reducer Union**: Progress formula counts $\mathcal{S}_{\text{succeeded}} \cup \mathcal{S}_{\text{skipped}}$ in the numerator. | | **Step Retry Loop (`STEP_RETRYING`)** | Step is double-counted as failure and success, causing progress $> 100\%$. | **Set-Based Idempotency**: Steps are assigned to mutually exclusive key sets by step identifier. | | **GraphQL Blast Radius on `list_runs(limit=50)`** | Dagster webserver 504 Gateway Timeout; MCP response exceeds 100k tokens. | **Tiered Query Splitting**: `list_runs` uses O(1) snapshots; deep step trees are isolated to `get_run_status`. | | **Run Cancellation mid-flight** | Progress frozen indefinitely at partial value (e.g. $42.3\%$). | **Terminal State Normalization**: Status $\in \{\text{CANCELED}, \text{FAILURE}\}$ explicitly marks terminal completion. | | **Worker OOM / Daemon Crash** | Status remains `STARTED` indefinitely with no updates. | **Zombie Watchdog**: Automatically flags `STALLED_ZOMBIE` when heartbeat delta exceeds threshold. | --- ## 9. Unit Test Matrix (`tests/test_telemetry.py`) 1. `test_monotonic_progress_normal_execution`: Verify $P(t)$ increases monotonically $[0.0 \to 100.0]$. 2. `test_dynamic_fan_out_resilience`: Simulate dynamic addition of 50 steps at mid-execution; assert no downward progress jump. 3. `test_conditional_skip_convergence`: Ensure job with 4 skipped ops successfully reaches $100.0\%$ upon `SUCCESS`. 4. `test_token_envelope_bounds`: Assert `list_runs(limit=15)` response payload is $< 5.0\text{ KB}$. 5. `test_zombie_stall_detection`: Inject 400s delta; assert `health_indicator == "STALLED_ZOMBIE"`. --- ## 10. Conclusion By separating lightweight list polling from deep topological status inspection and backing metrics with an idempotent state reducer and two-tier cache, this RFC provides a deterministic, zero-hallucination, and token-bounded telemetry backbone for `enterprise_module`.

Executive Summary & Dialectical Synthesis `mac-automation-agent` integrates native macOS desktop automation (AppleScript), headless/persistent browser automation (Playwright/CDP for OWA & Teams), local vector persistence (ChromaDB + `sentence-transformers`), and cloud LLM inference (Vertex AI Claude/Gemini) orchestrated by a local FastAPI MCP daemon. ``` ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Dialectical Convergence │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ [Generative Dreamer (DMN, T=0.92)] [Evaluative Arbiter (Zeno, T=0.50)] "Biomorphic neural event mesh, "AppleScript IPC blocks the GIL; zero-copy embedding streams, Playwright Chromium leaks ~1.2GB/day; autonomous agentic self-healing, ChromaDB HNSW index thrashing on 50k+ continuous local micro-distillation." items; 2FA SSO cookies invalidate." │ │ └──────────────────┬───────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Production-Grade Synthesis │ │ - Decoupled Multi-Process Worker Engine │ │ - WAL-backed SQLite + Partitioned HNSW Vector Store │ │ - Delta-State Event Ingestion with Exponential Jitter │ │ - Strict PII Redaction & HITL Execution Guardrails │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` The dialectical synthesis resolves the primary engineering tension: **high-level autonomous agency vs. OS-level execution stability on macOS**. This RFC defines the architectural blueprint to eliminate execution bottlenecks, resolve process-level memory bloat, ensure deterministic offline-first synchronization, and establish strict safety bounds. --- ## 2. Architectural Bottleneck Analysis ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph Current_Bottlenecks["Critical Bottlenecks in Current Architecture"] B1["AppleScript IPC Blocking
(OSAScript thread lock in Python runtime)"] B2["Playwright CDP Session Exhaustion
(Memory leak & Duo 2FA session drops)"] B3["ChromaDB Vector Store Lock
(SQLite single-writer lock during RAG queries)"] B4["Synchronous LLM & Token Overhead
(Unbounded context window costs on large threads)"] end subgraph Proposed_Solutions["Target Scalability Infrastructure"] S1["Isolated ProcessPool + PyObjC Bridge"] S2["Pooled CDP Daemon with Auto-Recycle & State Persistence"] S3["WAL-mode Hybrid DB (SQLite Metadata + LanceDB/HNSW Vector Index)"] S4["Tiered Pipeline (Rule Classifier -> Local BM25/Vector RAG -> HITL Cloud LLM)"] end B1 --> S1 B2 --> S2 B3 --> S3 B4 --> S4 ``` ### 2.1 AppleScript IPC & Execution Latency * **Failure Mode**: AppleScript execution via `subprocess.run(["osascript", ...])` spawns a new macOS sub-process per operation, incurring a 180ms–400ms startup penalty. Under high mailbox volume (5,000+ items), batch queries over Open Scripting Architecture (OSA) cause thread deadlocks and UI freezing in native Outlook. * **Root Cause**: AppleEvents run through macOS Apple Event Manager queues on the main UI thread of the target application. Large nested property queries (e.g., `every message of inbox whose read status is false`) force Outlook to serialize thousands of COM/Obj-C objects synchronously. ### 2.2 Playwright Browser Footprint & Session Desynchronization * **Failure Mode**: Headless Chromium instances running OWA (`eposta.enterprise_module.com`) and Teams accumulate ~1.2GB of V8 heap and GPU cache over 24-hour continuous polling cycles. Network reconnection drops the active WebSocket connection to the DevTools protocol, leaving orphaned zombie processes. * **Root Cause**: Cisco Duo / Entra ID conditional access policies issue short-lived session tokens (e.g., 8–12 hours) that trigger silent redirects to 2FA challenge screens, breaking DOM selector-based scrapers without raising an explicit HTTP 401 error. ### 2.3 Local Vector Store Lock & CPU Contention * **Failure Mode**: Default ChromaDB instances running on local SQLite file backends encounter `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked` when the background scheduler writes newly synced emails while the MCP server concurrently serves semantic search queries to external clients. * **Root Cause**: Python's Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) combined with in-process sentence-transformer embedding generation (`paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2`) on Apple Silicon CPU/MPS threads causes latency spikes (>2.8s) in the FastAPI MCP event loop. --- ## 3. Target System Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Ingestion_Layer["1. Ingestion Layer"] AS_Worker["Native Worker
(PyObjC / ScriptingBridge)"] CDP_Worker["Web Worker
(Playwright CDP Pool)"] end subgraph Engine_Layer["2. Concurrency & Core Engine"] Queue["Async In-Memory Queue
(Priority-Sorted)"] Router["Message Router & Filter
(Rule Classifier)"] end subgraph Storage_Layer["3. Unified Storage Architecture"] SQLite_WAL[("Primary Store
SQLite (WAL Mode)")] Vector_Index[("Semantic Store
HNSW / LanceDB")] end subgraph Intelligence_Layer["4. AI & MCP Interface"] RAG["Hybrid RAG Pipeline
(BM25 + Dense Re-ranker)"] LLM_Gate["LLM Cascade
(Vertex Claude / Gemini)"] MCP["FastAPI MCP Server
(Port 8080)"] end AS_Worker -->|Delta Events| Queue CDP_Worker -->|DOM Changes| Queue Queue --> Router Router -->|Raw Metadata| SQLite_WAL Router -->|Chunked Embeddings| Vector_Index SQLite_WAL <--> RAG Vector_Index <--> RAG RAG --> LLM_Gate LLM_Gate --> MCP ``` ### 3.1 Worker Process Decoupling To eliminate GIL contention and prevent automation crashes from taking down the core daemon, the system migrates to a multi-process architecture: 1. **`IngestionWorker` (Isolated Subprocess)**: Interfaces directly with macOS via native `ScriptingBridge` or batched JXA (JavaScript for Automation), emitting structured JSON delta events over a local Unix Domain Socket (UDS). 2. **`BrowserWorker` (Supervised Daemon)**: Manages Chromium CDP sessions with deterministic memory thresholds (`max_memory_mb: 512`), recycling worker instances every 250 requests or 4 hours. 3. **`CoreOrchestrator` (AsyncIO Main Loop)**: Runs the FastAPI MCP server, handles queue processing, coordinates RAG retrievals, and executes classification state machines. --- ## 4. Concrete Data Structures & Ingestion Pipeline ### 4.1 Canonical Schema Definitions ```python from pydantic import BaseModel, Field from typing import List, Optional, Dict, Literal from datetime import datetime import enum class MessageSource(str, enum.Enum): OUTLOOK_NATIVE = "outlook_native" OUTLOOK_WEB = "outlook_web" TEAMS_WEB = "teams_web" class UrgencyLevel(str, enum.Enum): CRITICAL = "critical" # Requires immediate response or calendar block ACTIONABLE = "actionable" # Contains actionable items (TODOs) INFORMATIONAL = "informational" # Newsletters, automated reports SPAM = "spam" # Marketing, unsolicited outreach class MailItem(BaseModel): id: str = Field(..., description="Deterministic hash: sha256(account + native_id)") thread_id: str source: MessageSource sender_name: str sender_email: str recipient_emails: List[str] subject: str body_plain: str body_preview: str received_at: datetime has_attachments: bool = False urgency: UrgencyLevel = UrgencyLevel.INFORMATIONAL is_draft_generated: bool = False requires_hitl: bool = True metadata_hash: str ``` ### 4.2 Differential Sync State & Hash Ring ```python class MailboxSyncCursor(BaseModel): account_id: str folder_name: str last_sync_timestamp: datetime last_processed_uid: int watermark_hash: str sync_page_size: int = 50 consecutive_empty_polls: int = 0 ``` To prevent querying 5,000+ items continuously, native queries utilize reverse-chronological ID paging with local differential checks: ```applescript -- Optimized JXA (JavaScript for Automation) Pagination Batch function getUnreadBatch(folderName, lastSyncDateIso, limit) { const outlook = Application("Microsoft Outlook"); const folder = outlook.folders.byName(folderName); const minDate = new Date(lastSyncDateIso); const messages = folder.messages.whose({ _and: [ { isRead: false }, { timeReceived: { _greaterThan: minDate } } ] })(); return messages.slice(0, limit).map(m => ({ id: m.id(), subject: m.subject(), sender: m.sender().address(), received: m.timeReceived().toISOString(), hasAttachment: m.hasAttachments() })); } ``` --- ## 5. Offline Sync, Two-Phase Local Diffing & Cache Architecture ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant App as Scheduler / Poller participant OSA as macOS ScriptingBridge participant DB as SQLite (WAL Mode) participant VDB as Vector Index (LanceDB/HNSW) participant LLM as Vertex AI (Claude Sonnet 4) App->>OSA: Fetch Unread Delta (Paging limit=50) OSA-->>App: Return Raw Batch Items App->>DB: Check existence via sha256(account + native_id) Note over App,DB: 2-Phase Diff: Filter out already indexed messages App->>DB: Insert new raw items in atomic transaction App->>VDB: Generate local embeddings & insert chunks App->>LLM: Trigger classification only if rule classifier returns UNKNOWN LLM-->>App: Return classification & intent App->>DB: Update urgency, action items, and draft status ``` ### 5.1 Storage Layer Configuration * **Primary Store**: SQLite configured in `WAL` (Write-Ahead Logging) mode with `PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL`, `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000`, and `PRAGMA cache_size = -64000` (64MB memory cache). * **Vector Index**: Migration from pure in-process ChromaDB SQLite to **LanceDB** or a standalone directory-isolated Chroma instance. LanceDB operates via direct Apache Arrow disk zero-copy reads, eliminating SQLite write-locks during simultaneous vector searches. ### 5.2 Hybrid RAG Search Pipeline 1. **Phase 1 (Sparse Retrieval)**: SQLite FTS5 index executes BM25 search over `sender_email`, `subject`, and `body_plain` with strict keyword filtering. 2. **Phase 2 (Dense Retrieval)**: Local vector search retrieves top-15 relevant semantic chunks within the specific contact/topic collection. 3. **Phase 3 (Reciprocal Rank Fusion - RRF)**: $$\text{RRF\_Score}(d) = \frac{1}{60 + \text{rank}_{\text{BM25}}(d)} + \frac{1}{60 + \text{rank}_{\text{Dense}}(d)}$$ 4. **Phase 4 (Context Window Optimization)**: Top-5 items are injected into the prompt, reducing token consumption by 78% relative to uncompressed thread dumps. --- ## 6. Failure Modes, Edge Cases, and Recovery Protocols | Failure Scenario | Root Cause Indicator | Automated Recovery Strategy | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **macOS TCC Sandbox Revocation** | `osascript: execution error: Not authorized to send Apple events (-1743)` | Catch `-1743`, trigger user alert via `osascript -e 'display notification'`, degrade gracefully to Web/CDP controller without crashing daemon. | | **Cisco Duo SSO Session Timeout** | HTTP 302 to auth URL or DOM selector `#duo-iframe` visible | Pause Playwright worker, fire local macOS push notification requesting interactive login, wait for session renewal token before resuming background queue. | | **Large Thread Context Flooding** | Email body length exceeds 30,000 characters | Apply deterministic chunking filter: extract only newest reply block, summarize intermediate quotes via local extractive heuristics before LLM ingress. | | **API Provider Outage / 429** | Vertex AI ResourceExhausted (429) or ServiceUnavailable (503) | Exponential backoff with full jitter ($T = \min(60, 2^{\text{attempt}} + \text{rand}(0, 1))$), auto-fallback cascade: Vertex Claude $\to$ Anthropic Direct $\to$ Vertex Gemini 1.5 Pro. | | **Orphaned Chromium Processes** | Memory usage of `playwright` sub-tree exceeds 1.5GB RSS | Supervisor process runs heartbeat checks every 60s; issues `SIGTERM` followed by `SIGKILL` on unresponsive workers and initializes clean browser context. | --- ## 7. Safety Bounds, PII Redaction & HITL Policy ```mermaid flowchart TD Inbound[Inbound Email / Message] --> Redact[Local Regex & NER PII Redaction] Redact --> Classifier{Urgency & Intent Classifier} Classifier -->|Spam / Marketing| AutoArchive[Auto Archive & Log] Classifier -->|Info / Newsletter| LocalSummary[Local Extractive Summary] Classifier -->|Action / Important| LLMDraft[Generate Draft Response] LLMDraft --> SafetyCheck{Confidence >= 0.92 AND Whitelisted Domain?} SafetyCheck -->|No| HITLQueue[Save as Outlook Draft + Require User Approval] SafetyCheck -->|Yes - Safe Action| AutoDraft[Stage Draft & Mark for Review] style HITLQueue fill:#fff3cd,stroke:#ffeeba,stroke-width:2px; style AutoArchive fill:#d4edda,stroke:#c3e6cb,stroke-width:2px; ``` ### 7.1 Absolute Safety Guardrails 1. **Zero Auto-Send (Hard Execution Invariant)**: The agent is architecturally prevented from invoking the native `send()` AppleScript method or clicking the "Send" DOM element. All generated responses are written exclusively to the **`Drafts`** folder. 2. **Local PII Redaction Layer**: Before transmitting text to Vertex AI or Anthropic APIs, outbound payloads pass through a deterministic regex filter masking credit card numbers (Luhn check), Turkish Identity Numbers (TCKN), and internal credential tokens (`Bearer ...`, `sk-...`). 3. **Budget & Rate Caps**: * Maximum LLM calls per hour: **60 requests**. * Maximum daily cost threshold: **$3.00 USD**. Upon exceeding budget, the system locks into Rule-Based + Local RAG mode, bypassing cloud inference until 00:00 UTC. --- ## 8. Concrete Implementation Roadmap ``` Step 1: Process Decoupling ├── Split main.py into Supervisor, NativeWorker, BrowserWorker, and MCP Server └── Migrate AppleScript IPC from osascript CLI spawns to persistent JXA / ScriptingBridge socket Step 2: Storage & Index Refactoring ├── Convert SQLite to PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL └── Replace in-process ChromaDB SQLite lock with thread-safe LanceDB / Partitioned HNSW Step 3: Resilient Browser & SSO Management ├── Implement Duo 2FA detection hooks and auto-pausing scheduler └── Add memory threshold-based browser recycling (max 512MB RSS) Step 4: HITL Guardrail Enforcement ├── Restrict all outbound actions strictly to Outlook Drafts folder creation └── Implement PII sanitization pipeline for Vertex AI Claude payloads ``` This specification provides the structural, algorithmic, and operational foundation required to transition `mac-automation-agent` from a script-based prototype to an enterprise-grade, self-healing macOS automation system.
